dedupe_keys.name: google cloud and oracle london data centre outages in the july 2022 heatwave

description: This post-event case records how the record heat of 19 July 2022, when eastern England reached 40.3 degrees Celsius, knocked out cloud data centres in London. Google reported a simultaneous failure of multiple redundant cooling systems in one of the buildings hosting its europe-west2-a zone, which could no longer keep a safe temperature and was partly powered down, affecting several Google Cloud services for many hours; Oracle said two cooling units in its UK South region failed when they had to run above their design limits, and some customers took about 19 hours to regain access. A London hospital trust also lost IT systems to overheating the same day. Coverage: London cloud regions of Google and Oracle, 19 to 20 July 2022. Format and access: Google's incident report on its cloud status page and Oracle statements, summarised free by the trade press. Caveats: operators disclosed little about design limits or plant; the heatwave was forecast, so the case also reflects preparedness choices. Simulation uses: hazard exposure of data-centre cooling to extreme heat, fragility thresholds of chillers and dry coolers as ambient temperature rises, and climate adaptation of design temperatures. Related records: the techUK adaptation report and XDI climate-risk analysis look at the same risk, and the Azure Australia East and Singapore Equinix cases are other cooling failures.
